questions.question: What is the octet rule? What are its limitations?
questions.solution:
**Octet rule:** atoms tend to combine in such a way that each has eight electrons in its valence shell, attaining noble-gas configuration.

**Limitations:**
- Incomplete octet: BeCl₂, BF₃ (central atom has only 4/6 electrons).
- Expanded octet: SF₆, PCl₅ (10 or 12 electrons around central atom).
- Odd-electron molecules: NO, NO₂ cannot satisfy the rule.
- It says nothing about shape, relative stability or energy of molecules.

questions.question: Calculate the number of molecules and moles present in 5.6 L of oxygen gas at STP.
What is a homologous series? State any two characteristics.
questions.solution:
A **homologous series** is a family of organic compounds with the same general formula, same functional group and similar chemical properties, whose successive members differ by –CH₂– unit.

**Characteristics:** (i) members can be prepared by similar methods; (ii) physical properties change gradually with molecular mass; (iii) consecutive members differ by 14 in molecular mass.

questions.question: Why is the electron affinity of chlorine higher than that of fluorine?
questions.solution: Fluorine's valence shell (2p) is very compact — an incoming electron feels strong repulsion from the already present electrons. Chlorine's 3p shell is larger, so the added electron experiences much less repulsion despite lower electronegativity. Hence Cl has a **higher (more negative) electron affinity** than F.
